item.name: Service
item.description: Service health and API contract endpoints.

request.description: Checks that the API process is alive. This endpoint has no database dependency.
Checks that the API can reach PostgreSQL. A 503 response means the process is alive but the database is unavailable.
Fetches the generated API contract used by Swagger UI and client tooling.
Creates one-time state and nonce values and returns Google's authorization URL with only openid, email, and profile scopes.
Exchanges a Google authorization code, validates signature/issuer/audience/state/nonce/verified-email claims, and creates a normal StudyFlow session.
Confirms a server-issued, one-time Google identity challenge with the matching account password, attaches the identity, and creates a normal session.
Confirms account linking with the short-lived HttpOnly challenge cookie created by the browser callback.

exec: pm.test('returns HTTP 200 or expired challenge 401', () => pm.expect([200, 401]).to.include(pm.response.code));

request.description: Lists the authenticated account's linked Google identity without exposing provider tokens.
Sends an eight-hour single-use verification link when eligible. No account or password is created before verification. The response is intentionally non-enumerating.

exec: pm.expect(body.message).to.eql('Check your email to continue registration if the address is eligible.');

request.description: Authenticates a verified password account, sets the secure opaque session cookie, and returns the CSRF token.
Validates the opaque session cookie and refreshes its idle expiry.
Validates CSRF, revokes the server session, and clears both browser cookies.
Returns a non-enumerating response and rotates the verification token for an eligible unverified account.
Returns a non-enumerating response and sends a one-hour reset link when the verified password account is eligible.
Consumes the one-hour single-use token, updates the password, and revokes all existing sessions.
Consumes an unexpired single-use token and returns a 30-minute signup token.
Creates the account only after the email was verified; the signup token is short-lived and single-use.
Returns the authenticated student's immutable ID and email plus editable display name.
Updates only the authenticated student's profile name and requires the session-bound CSRF token.
Returns the account timezone, session length, break preference, and whether recurring availability needs reconfirmation.
Updates validated planning preferences. A timezone change marks recurring availability for confirmation without changing stored deadline instants.
Verifies the current password, applies breach and Argon2id policy to the replacement, then revokes all sessions.
Creates a task owned by the authenticated student. Planned duration initially equals the original estimate.

exec: pm.test('generated task deadline is a valid future instant', () => {

request.description: Lists only owned tasks, ordered by deadline. Supports Course, Category, Priority, and deadline-range filters; Task Status is added with lifecycle derivation.
Returns one owned task. Missing and cross-user identifiers both return 404.
Replaces editable fields, preserves deadline history, and rejects estimate changes after work starts.
Idempotently starts an owned task and freezes its original estimate.
Explicitly confirms early completion while preserving work history.
Deletes the owned task and cascading task history only after explicit confirmation.

item.name: Schedule Proposals
item.description: Authenticated generation, preview, acceptance, and rejection of inactive schedule proposals.

request.description: Generates and stores an inactive proposal from the authenticated student's current tasks and availability.
Runs a one-off scenario without persisting a proposal or changing the active schedule. Temporary availability and blocks do not alter recurring availability.
Returns the authenticated student's current inactive proposal with sessions, unscheduled work, and overload details.
Accepts the complete feasible proposal and atomically replaces the active future schedule.
Rejects the inactive proposal without changing the active schedule. Acceptance and rejection are alternative actions.

item.name: Availability
item.description: Authenticated recurring weekly availability in the account timezone.

request.description: Lists the authenticated student's canonical recurring weekly availability.
Atomically creates, updates, or deletes the complete owned weekly availability set and merges touching windows.
Confirms that local-time availability remains correct after a timezone change.

Atomically applies grouped study preferences and recurring availability changes in one transaction. Blocked-period adds, updates, removals, and timezone confirmation can be included in the same request.
Lists owned dated exceptions in absolute UTC instants.
Creates an owned dated exception and reports future sessions invalidated by it.
Updates one owned exception; missing and cross-user IDs both return 404.
Deletes one owned exception after explicit confirmation.

item.name: Scheduling
item.description: Generate, inspect, accept, and recover study schedules.

request.description: Lists the authenticated student's accepted, non-invalidated Study Sessions. Optional from and to timestamps use an inclusive-start, exclusive-end overlap range; task_id narrows the result to one Academic Task.

Records Missed and returns the inactive recovery revision preview. Repeating this request retries recovery for an unresolved Missed outcome without duplicating it; a no-longer-valid trigger returns 409 and oversized recovery input returns 422. A solver failure returns 503 after preserving the outcome.
